headline: Databricks settles on $5B raise at $190B valuation, after investors sought $15B
summary: Databricks initially sought $1 billion, but overwhelming investor interest led to a $5 billion raise, pushing its valuation to $190 billion.
details: AI big-data firm Databricks initially sought to raise $1 billion. However, overwhelming investor interest quickly swelled to $15 billion. The company ultimately settled on a $5 billion funding round, pushing its valuation to $190 billion.

The surge in interest was partly accidental, following a news report during the company's conference. This turned into a self-fulfilling prophecy, with a "long line of investors" calling, eager to participate in the deal.

Databricks' strong financials underpin this demand. The company boasts $7 billion in annualized run rate revenue, growing at 80%, and is cash-flow positive. Its core cloud data warehouse product alone accounts for $1.5 billion ARR, growing at 100% year-over-year.
The "AI pixie dust" also plays a significant role. Products like Lakebase, its database for agents, already hit $100 million ARR, and its AI chatbot tool, Genie, is "insanely popular."
Despite previous large raises, the new capital is crucial for AI investments. Databricks faces multibillion-dollar cloud commitments with hyperscalers and funds a 100-person AI research team.
The company is also active in mergers and acquisitions, having recently acquired Electric (PGlite) and Panther, an AI cybersecurity firm, among others. This M&A strategy requires significant capital.

While Databricks has become a "meme" for its extensive private fundraising, CEO Ali Ghodsi still aims for an IPO one day. For now, investing heavily in AI out of the public eye seems a strategic move, especially with such high investor demand.
